compare degree and pattern of division

learner_visual_status.note: One verified exact-species photo is a temporary anchor; diagnostic bract-tier photos remain priority.

synonyms: Anemone caroliniana Torr. & A.Gray (1838; illegitimate later homonym, NOT Anemone caroliniana Walter 1788)
taxonomic_note: Accepted Anemone berlandieri Pritz. Do not merge with accepted A. caroliniana Walter; the later illegitimate homonym A. caroliniana Torr. & A.Gray refers to this taxon.
look_here_first: On a flowering plant, photograph the entire scape: ONE tier of three leaflike involucral bracts sits ABOVE the scape midpoint. Then compare multiple basal leaves to that bract tier: all basal leaves are divided differently from the bracts. Flowers alone are not enough.

project_inclusion.learner_admission_basis: Master Plant Pool row 71, 2 source flags; existing reviewed taxonomy/diagnostics dated 2026-10-09
project_inclusion.range_basis: POWO/FNA accept species and support Texas nativity at state scale; three distinct project target-zone county proofs have not been audited. No confirmed-target-native metric credit.

morphology_keys.habit: Herbaceous spring perennial from underground tuber; flowering stalk (scape) with one showy terminal flower.
morphology_keys.leaves: Basal leaves deeply divided; compare several basal leaves with involucral bracts rather than relying on leaflet outline alone.
morphology_keys.involucre: Single tier of three leaflike bracts above the midpoint of the flowering scape; basal leaves dissimilar in division.
morphology_keys.flower: Numerous narrow petal-like SEPALS, not true petals; white/pink/purple variation overlaps related species.
morphology_keys.fruit: Aggregate head of achenes; mature achenes densely woolly; close-up useful as secondary evidence.
best_field_traits: one involucral-bract tier ABOVE scape midpoint
all basal leaves divided differently from bracts
single terminal flower with petaloid sepals

comparisons.key_distinctions: A. caroliniana Walter has ONE bract tier BELOW midpoint and at least one basal leaf similar to the bracts. A. edwardsiana has TWO bract tiers. Sepal count and flower color overlap and must not substitute for scape/bract evidence.
